newsitem.title: USA: FedEx says surcharge will offset high costs.
newsitem.headline: FedEx says surcharge will offset high costs.

text.p: An official at Federal Express Corp said the company's announced surcharge will help it offset higher operating costs in upcoming quarters.

"The surcharge...will impact our revenues and help us offset the costs associated (with high fuel prices,") said Alan B. Graf, Jr., executive vice president and chief financial officer, in a conference call with reporters.
In its fiscal second quarter earnings release, Federal Express said it will add a temporary two percent surcharge to all express package shipments due to "stubbornly high" fuel prices.
The surcharge will not take effect until February 3 and will apply to all shipments tendered within the United States, as well as U.S. export shipments, except those to China and Hong Kong.
Shares of Federal Express fell 2-1/2 to close at 40-1/8 in New York Stock Exchange trading.
Graf said high jet fuel prices added about $25 million to the fiscal second quarter's operating expense. "That's $100 million on an annualized basis...we simply cannot afford to absorb all that."

He also said he is not certain if fuel prices will come down in the near future. "The futures market is telling us (that jet fuel prices) will come down. I'm not so sure that's true...we have to be cautious."
The surcharge will be a flat two percent charge that will be particular to each customer's rate scale, he said.
Separately, Graf said he had a rosy outlook toward the international market.
The company reported 17 percent growth in the quarter in its International Priority express package volumes. "I'm very optimistic about international performance," Graf said.
International Priority package revenues account for more than 20 percent of Federal Express' total express package revenue.
